Chapter 5: The Power of Environment and Association.
Have you ever noticed how much the people around you, and the places you spend time in, can shape your life—especially when it comes to money? It’s a bit like how plants either thrive or struggle, depending on the soil and climate they’re in. Your financial habits and beliefs are being shaped, every day, by the company you keep and the environments you choose.
People who consistently find financial success usually make a deliberate choice: they surround themselves with others who share the same drive and values. Now, that doesn’t mean you have to distance yourself from old friends or family. What it really means is being open to building new connections that push you to grow. When you’re around folks who think big, take action, and lift each other up, it’s amazing how much more motivated and inspired you’ll feel.
And let’s not forget about your environment. Spending time in places that radiate abundance—like a buzzing business, a community of entrepreneurs, or even just a tidy, inviting home—can really reinforce the habits and beliefs that support your financial goals. On the flip side, if you’re surrounded by negativity, chaos, or a sense of scarcity, it’s a lot tougher to keep a wealth-oriented mindset.
So, how can you start building a more supportive environment? Here are a few simple ideas:
Try joining groups or organizations that focus on personal and financial growth. Make time for events, workshops, or seminars where you can learn and connect with others. Be intentional about what you read, watch, or listen to—choose books, podcasts, and news that emphasize success and possibility. And take a look at your physical space: does it feel organized, inspiring, and abundant?
Picture this: if you’re dreaming of starting a business, you might join a local entrepreneur group, show up at networking events, or find someone to be your accountability partner. These relationships do more than offer practical advice—they give you encouragement and perspective, especially when things get tough.
It’s also worth paying attention to the messages you get from the media and culture around you. We’re all soaked in stories about money and success, but not all of them are helpful—or even true. Choosing to focus on examples of growth, resilience, and real achievement can help drown out the negativity and build up your confidence.
In the end, your environment acts as both a mirror and a catalyst. It shows you where you’re at, but it can also give you the support you need to grow and change. When you intentionally shape the people and places that are part of your everyday life, you’ll find it’s a whole lot easier to stay focused on your financial goals and move steadily toward abundance.
